ECE 6390 / Antennas and arrays

Planar steering

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how a plane of equal-amplitude elements steers in two directional coordinates.

For an aperture normal to z, direction cosines are u = sin θ cos φ and v = sin θ sin φ. Physical directions on a hemisphere satisfy u² + v² ≤ 1.

On a λ/2 rectangular grid, a steering phase ramp φmn = −π(mu₀ + nv₀) cancels path phase in direction (u₀, v₀). The resulting uniform-grid array factor separates into x and y sums.

Increasing aperture extent in x narrows variation in u, while y extent controls v. The displayed coherent-peak normalization shows beam shape. Absolute intensity, spherical integration, element pattern, and efficiency are needed for an absolute gain or link claim.

Example

Steering to u₀ = 0.2 and v₀ = −0.1 requires phase steps of −36° per x element and +18° per y element for λ/2 spacing.

Model and course sources

    Practice

    1. For a large uniform grid near boresight, what happens to the u and v beamwidths if only the x extent approximately doubles?

    Each separable factor is controlled mainly by its own aperture dimension.

    The u beamwidth roughly halves, while the v beamwidth stays similar. The active-element count and absolute power normalization must be handled separately.
